meaning: Stripe rejected the secret key your server sent. It may be wrong, revoked, cut off, from another account, or you sent the publishable key where a secret key belongs.
causes: Env var empty or not set in the hosting environment (so the code sends 'undefined').
The publishable key (pk_) used on the server instead of the secret key (sk_ or rk_).
Key was rolled/revoked in the Dashboard.
Extra quotes or spaces pasted into the env var.

steps.text: Never put the secret key in frontend code. On the server, read it from env and fail loudly if missing.
In Stripe Dashboard > Developers > API keys, reveal or create a key in the right mode and paste it without quotes.
Set it in the place your code runs: Vercel/Netlify env settings, Supabase secrets (supabase secrets set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=...), or Replit Secrets. Redeploy after changing env vars.
If a secret key was ever committed or pasted into a chat, roll it in the Dashboard.

prompt: Stripe returns 'Invalid API Key provided'. Make sure the Stripe secret key is only used server-side from process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (or Deno.env in Edge Functions), add a startup check that it starts with sk_ or rk_, remove any secret key from frontend code, and use only the publishable key (pk_) in the browser.

faq.q: Which key goes in the frontend?
I changed the env var but nothing changed?
faq.a: Most hosts need a redeploy to pick up new env vars.
